text:
Nina R: Quick RFC follow-up - PR feedback asked for a clear "decision-plane" contract. We should lock this down so host agents, observer, and SRE tooling all align.

Victor T: Draft constraints: decisions must be monotonic (seq), have an effective window (lease), and carry a GC hint. Hosts accept only seq > last_seen and within lease.

Samir P: Agreed. Also need a lightweight local-override token that hosts can emit when they detect transient SLO violations. Tokens are short-lived and don't change long-term plan unless aggregated.

Elena J: Propose shapes. Example plan (planner -> hosts):

```json
{"plan_id": "pl-20260323-01", "seq": 128, "assignments": {"region-a": "v2", "region-b": "v1"}, "effective_until": "2026-03-23T16:40:00Z", "gc_after": "2026-03-23T16:45:00Z", "meta": {"reason": "intent-789", "author": "team-x"}}
```

Samir P: And local fallback token (host -> planner):

```json
{"host": "host-42", "seq_seen": 128, "reason_code": "SLOW_MODEL", "ttl_seconds": 30, "backoff_ms": 5000}
```

Nina R: Important semantics: planner SHOULD ignore isolated tokens, but MUST escalate if X% of hosts in a shard emit the same reason within window W. Those thresholds are configurable per-service.

Victor T: Sequence enforcement: hosts store last_seq and last_plan_id. When planner reconnects, it sends latest plan; hosts call accept if plan.seq > last_seq OR plan.plan_id != last_plan_id. This prevents stale replays after GC.

Elena J: For metric smoothing, default window = 60s and default smoothing = EWMA alpha 0.2. Teams can request shorter windows but require a justification field in the intent and an ops approval gate for <30s.

Samir P: For hysteresis and re-enable: local fallback uses exponential backoff (start 5s, double up to 2m). Also hosts should attach a "cooldown_until" to the token to help planner observe re-enable attempts.

Victor T: Edge case: planner downtime. Hosts must continue honoring last valid plan until effective_until + grace (default 5m). If both planner and last plan expire, hosts fall back to safe default (configured per-service, e.g., stable variant).

Nina R: Security + ops: APIs must require client_request_id and idempotency token for plan changes. Overrides require RBAC and be logged. Every decision record stored in audit store with who/why/diff.

Elena J: SRE asks for a probe websocket: `/ws/plans/stream` that emits plan events and local token aggregations. Add `probe_port` read-only access for on-call.

Samir P: Telemetry: include reason_code enum: ["CPU_STALL","OOM","NET_ERR","KV_MISS","SLOW_MODEL","DISK_IO"]. Add an optional diagnostics blob but scrub PII.

Victor T: GC: planner emits gc_after. Hosts GC local state only after gc_after + jitter. Planner also exposes `/plans?expired=true` for operators to inspect stale plans before GC.

Nina R: Ops runbook snippets we should include in RFC follow-up: local token TTL=30s, backoff start=5s, max backoff=120s, planner eval window=60s, escalation threshold default=10% of shard. These are tunable.

Elena J: Quick compatibility note: older agents lacking seq-check should accept plan if plan_id differs; we must include a compatibility header and a deprecation timeline.

ops-bot: Planner applied plan 1867772026 at 2026-03-23T16:10Z (seq=128) :white_check_mark:

Samir P: I'll add a minimal host shim with seq accept/reject logic and local token emitter POC to the agent repo.

Victor T: I'll draft the planner API swagger and the websocket event schema.

Nina R: Great. Once PRs land we'll fold concrete numbers into the RFC and add RBAC/audit tickets. Thanks all.
